back: Sorghum, pearl millet and finger millet: small-seeded cereals adapted to hot, dry conditions.
Extensive fibrous roots, waxy bloom, leaf rolling, dormancy in drought and recovery after rain, short season.

front: Which natural regions suit small grains?
back: Mainly regions IV and V (sorghum also III); maize is risky there.
Rotate with non-host crops, pull before flowering, add manure and nitrogen, tolerant cultivars.

front: Reducing bird damage to small grains
back: Brown high-tannin cultivars, synchronised early planting, bird scaring, prompt harvest.
Irrigated winter crop: planted late April to May, harvested September to October before the rains; seed about 100-120 kg/ha.
Litres = area in m² × depth in mm; m³ = litres ÷ 1,000.
A side shoot from the base of a cereal plant that can carry its own ear or head.
Young or drought-stressed sorghum can release prussic acid (hydrogen cyanide) and poison livestock.
